solution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer \(x^2-y^2=cx\) solves a different (opposite-sign) equation; the correct solution is \(x^3-3xy^2=c\) (below).]

The equation \((x^2 - y^2)\,dx - 2xy\,dy = 0\) is homogeneous.

Write \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{2xy}\).

Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 - v^2x^2}{2vx^2} = \dfrac{1 - v^2}{2v}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - v^2}{2v} - v = \dfrac{1 - v^2 - 2v^2}{2v} = \dfrac{1 - 3v^2}{2v}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{2v}{1 - 3v^2}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Integrate. For the left side, let \(t = 1 - 3v^2\), \(dt = -6v\,dv\), so \(2v\,dv = -\dfrac{1}{3}dt\):
\(\int \dfrac{2v}{1 - 3v^2}\,dv = -\dfrac{1}{3}\log|1 - 3v^2|\).

Hence
\(-\dfrac{1}{3}\log|1 - 3v^2| = \log|x| + c_1\).

Multiply by \(-3\):
\(\log|1 - 3v^2| = -3\log|x| + c_2\).

So \(|1 - 3v^2|\,|x|^3 = c\). Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\):
\(\left(1 - \dfrac{3y^2}{x^2}\right)x^3 = c\), i.e. \(x(x^2 - 3y^2) = c\).

The general solution is \(x^3 - 3xy^2 = c\).

The equation is \(\left(1 + 2e^{x/y}\right) + 2e^{x/y}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{y}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

Write it in the form
\(\left(1 + 2e^{x/y}\right)dx + 2e^{x/y}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{y}\right)dy = 0\).

This is homogeneous in \(x\) and \(y\) (degree 0). Since \(\dfrac{x}{y}\) appears, put \(x = vy\), so \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy}\).

From the equation, \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = -\,\dfrac{2e^{v}\left(1 - v\right)}{1 + 2e^{v}}\) (using \(\dfrac{x}{y} = v\)).

So
\(v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{2e^{v}(1 - v)}{1 + 2e^{v}}\).

Then
\(y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{2e^{v}(1 - v)}{1 + 2e^{v}} - v = \dfrac{-2e^{v}(1 - v) - v(1 + 2e^{v})}{1 + 2e^{v}}\).

Simplify the numerator:
\(-2e^{v} + 2ve^{v} - v - 2ve^{v} = -2e^{v} - v = -(v + 2e^{v})\).

So
\(y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{v + 2e^{v}}{1 + 2e^{v}}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{1 + 2e^{v}}{v + 2e^{v}}\,dv = -\dfrac{dy}{y}\).

The numerator \(1 + 2e^{v}\) is exactly the derivative of the denominator \(v + 2e^{v}\). Integrating,
\(\log|v + 2e^{v}| = -\log|y| + c_1\).

Hence \(|v + 2e^{v}|\,|y| = c\). Replace \(v = \dfrac{x}{y}\):
\(\left(\dfrac{x}{y} + 2e^{x/y}\right)y = c\).

The general solution is \(x + 2y\,e^{x/y} = c\).

The equation \(y^2\,dx + (xy + x^2)\,dy = 0\) is homogeneous.

Write \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y^2}{xy + x^2}\).

Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{v^2x^2}{vx^2 + x^2} = -\dfrac{v^2}{v + 1}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{v^2}{v + 1} - v = \dfrac{-v^2 - v(v + 1)}{v + 1} = \dfrac{-2v^2 - v}{v + 1} = -\dfrac{v(2v + 1)}{v + 1}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{v + 1}{v(2v + 1)}\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Resolve into partial fractions:
\(\dfrac{v + 1}{v(2v + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{v} + \dfrac{B}{2v + 1}\).
Then \(v + 1 = A(2v + 1) + Bv\). Put \(v = 0\): \(1 = A\). Put \(v = -\tfrac12\): \(\tfrac12 = -\tfrac12 B\), so \(B = -1\).

Hence
\(\int\left(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{2v + 1}\right)dv = -\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\).
\(\log|v| - \dfrac{1}{2}\log|2v + 1| = -\log|x| + c_1\).

Multiply by 2:
\(2\log|v| - \log|2v + 1| = -2\log|x| + c_2\), i.e. \(\log\dfrac{v^2 x^2}{2v + 1} = c_2\).

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\): \(v^2 x^2 = y^2\) and \(2v + 1 = \dfrac{2y + x}{x}\), so
\(\dfrac{y^2}{(2y + x)/x} = c\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x y^2}{2y + x} = c\).

The general solution is \(x y^2 = c\,(x + 2y)\).

The equation \((x^2 - y^2)\,dx + 2xy\,dy = 0\) is homogeneous.

Write \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{2xy} = \dfrac{y^2 - x^2}{2xy}\).

Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v^2x^2 - x^2}{2vx^2} = \dfrac{v^2 - 1}{2v}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v^2 - 1}{2v} - v = \dfrac{v^2 - 1 - 2v^2}{2v} = \dfrac{-(1 + v^2)}{2v}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{2v}{1 + v^2}\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Integrate (numerator is the derivative of \(1 + v^2\)):
\(\log(1 + v^2) = -\log|x| + c_1\).

Hence \((1 + v^2)\,|x| = c\). Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\):
\(\left(1 + \dfrac{y^2}{x^2}\right)x = c\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x} = c\).

The general solution is \(x^2 + y^2 = c\,x\).

The equation is \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x - 2y}{2x - y} = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x - 2y}{2x - y} = \dfrac{2y - x}{2x - y}\).

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{2vx - x}{2x - vx} = \dfrac{2v - 1}{2 - v}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{2v - 1}{2 - v} - v = \dfrac{2v - 1 - v(2 - v)}{2 - v} = \dfrac{2v - 1 - 2v + v^2}{2 - v} = \dfrac{v^2 - 1}{2 - v}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{2 - v}{v^2 - 1}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Resolve the left side. Write \(\dfrac{2 - v}{(v - 1)(v + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{v - 1} + \dfrac{B}{v + 1}\).
Then \(2 - v = A(v + 1) + B(v - 1)\). Put \(v = 1\): \(1 = 2A\), so \(A = \tfrac12\). Put \(v = -1\): \(3 = -2B\), so \(B = -\tfrac32\).

Integrate:
\(\dfrac{1}{2}\log|v - 1| - \dfrac{3}{2}\log|v + 1| = \log|x| + c_1\).

Multiply by 2:
\(\log|v - 1| - 3\log|v + 1| = 2\log|x| + c_2\), i.e. \(\log\dfrac{|v - 1|}{|v + 1|^3} = 2\log|x| + c_2\).

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\): \(v - 1 = \dfrac{y - x}{x}\), \(v + 1 = \dfrac{y + x}{x}\), so
\(\dfrac{(y - x)/x}{(y + x)^3/x^3} = c\,x^2\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2(y - x)}{(y + x)^3} = c\,x^2\).

The general solution is \(\dfrac{y - x}{(x + y)^3} = c\), i.e. \(y - x = c\,(x + y)^3\).

The equation is \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y + x\sin\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = 0\), i.e.
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} - \sin\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\).

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v - \sin v\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\sin v\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{dv}{\sin v} = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\), i.e. \(\csc v\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Integrate. Since \(\int \csc v\,dv = \log\left|\tan\dfrac{v}{2}\right|\):
\(\log\left|\tan\dfrac{v}{2}\right| = -\log|x| + c_1\).

Hence \(\left|\tan\dfrac{v}{2}\right|\,|x| = c\). Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\):

The general solution is \(x\,\tan\left(\dfrac{y}{2x}\right) = c\).

The equation is \(\left(1 + e^{x/y}\right)dx + e^{x/y}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{y}\right)dy = 0\).

This is homogeneous (degree 0) with \(\dfrac{x}{y}\) appearing, so put \(x = vy\), so \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy}\).

From the equation,
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = -\dfrac{e^{v}(1 - v)}{1 + e^{v}}\).

So
\(v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{e^{v}(1 - v)}{1 + e^{v}}\).

Then
\(y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{e^{v}(1 - v)}{1 + e^{v}} - v = \dfrac{-e^{v}(1 - v) - v(1 + e^{v})}{1 + e^{v}}\).

Simplify the numerator:
\(-e^{v} + ve^{v} - v - ve^{v} = -e^{v} - v = -(v + e^{v})\).

So
\(y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{v + e^{v}}{1 + e^{v}}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{1 + e^{v}}{v + e^{v}}\,dv = -\dfrac{dy}{y}\).

The numerator \(1 + e^{v}\) is the derivative of the denominator \(v + e^{v}\). Integrating,
\(\log|v + e^{v}| = -\log|y| + c_1\).

Hence \(|v + e^{v}|\,|y| = c\). Replace \(v = \dfrac{x}{y}\):
\(\left(\dfrac{x}{y} + e^{x/y}\right)y = c\).

The general solution is \(x + y\,e^{x/y} = c\).

The equation is \(y^2 - x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = xy\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Collect the \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) terms:
\(y^2 = xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (xy + x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

So
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2}{x^2 + xy}\).

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v^2x^2}{x^2 + vx^2} = \dfrac{v^2}{1 + v}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v^2}{1 + v} - v = \dfrac{v^2 - v(1 + v)}{1 + v} = \dfrac{-v}{1 + v}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{1 + v}{v}\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{1}{v} + 1\right)dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Integrate:
\(\log|v| + v = -\log|x| + c\).

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\):
\(\log\left|\dfrac{y}{x}\right| + \dfrac{y}{x} = -\log|x| + c\), i.e. \(\log|y| - \log|x| + \dfrac{y}{x} + \log|x| = c\).

The general solution is \(\log|y| + \dfrac{y}{x} = c\).

The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^3 - 3\) is linear in \(y\), with \(P = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(Q = x^3 - 3\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int P\,dx} = e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx} = e^{\log x} = x\).

The solution is
\(y\cdot x = \int (x^3 - 3)\,x\,dx + c = \int (x^4 - 3x)\,dx + c\).

Integrate:
\(xy = \dfrac{x^5}{5} - \dfrac{3x^2}{2} + c\).

The general solution is \(xy = \dfrac{x^5}{5} - \dfrac{3x^2}{2} + c\).

The equation is \(\cos^2 x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = \tan x\).

Divide by \(\cos^2 x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{\cos^2 x} = \dfrac{\tan x}{\cos^2 x}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (\sec^2 x)\,y = \tan x\sec^2 x\).

This is linear with \(P = \sec^2 x\), \(Q = \tan x\sec^2 x\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \sec^2 x\,dx} = e^{\tan x}\).

The solution is
\(y\,e^{\tan x} = \int \tan x\sec^2 x\;e^{\tan x}\,dx + c\).

Put \(t = \tan x\), \(dt = \sec^2 x\,dx\):
\(\int t\,e^{t}\,dt = e^{t}(t - 1) = e^{\tan x}(\tan x - 1)\).

Hence
\(y\,e^{\tan x} = e^{\tan x}(\tan x - 1) + c\).

The general solution is \(y = \tan x - 1 + c\,e^{-\tan x}\).

The equation \((x + 2y^3)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\) is not linear in \(y\), but it is linear in \(x\).

Write
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x + 2y^3}{y} = \dfrac{x}{y} + 2y^2\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1}{y}\,x = 2y^2\).

This is linear in \(x\) with \(P = -\dfrac{1}{y}\), \(Q = 2y^2\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -\frac{1}{y}dy} = e^{-\log y} = \dfrac{1}{y}\).

The solution is
\(x\cdot\dfrac{1}{y} = \int 2y^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{y}\,dy + c = \int 2y\,dy + c = y^2 + c\).

The general solution is \(\dfrac{x}{y} = y^2 + c\), i.e. \(x = y^3 + c\,y\).

The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\sec x = \tan x\) is linear with \(P = \sec x\), \(Q = \tan x\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \sec x\,dx} = e^{\log|\sec x + \tan x|} = \sec x + \tan x\).

The solution is
\(y(\sec x + \tan x) = \int \tan x\,(\sec x + \tan x)\,dx + c\).

Compute the integral:
\(\int (\tan x\sec x + \tan^2 x)\,dx = \int \tan x\sec x\,dx + \int (\sec^2 x - 1)\,dx\)
\(= \sec x + \tan x - x\).

Hence the general solution is
\(y(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec x + \tan x - x + c\).

The equation is \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = x^2\log x\).

Divide by \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2}{x}\,y = x\log x\).

This is linear with \(P = \dfrac{2}{x}\), \(Q = x\log x\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx} = e^{2\log x} = x^2\).

The solution is
\(y\,x^2 = \int x\log x\cdot x^2\,dx + c = \int x^3\log x\,dx + c\).

Integrate by parts with \(u = \log x\), \(dv = x^3\,dx\):
\(\int x^3\log x\,dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \int \dfrac{x^4}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \dfrac{1}{4}\int x^3\,dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \dfrac{x^4}{16}\).

Hence the general solution is
\(x^2 y = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \dfrac{x^4}{16} + c\).

The equation \((x + y)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\) is not linear in \(y\), but it is linear in \(x\).

Write
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x + y\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} - x = y\).

This is linear in \(x\) with \(P = -1\), \(Q = y\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -1\,dy} = e^{-y}\).

The solution is
\(x\,e^{-y} = \int y\,e^{-y}\,dy + c\).

Integrate by parts:
\(\int y\,e^{-y}\,dy = -y\,e^{-y} + \int e^{-y}\,dy = -y\,e^{-y} - e^{-y} = -(y + 1)e^{-y}\).

Hence
\(x\,e^{-y} = -(y + 1)e^{-y} + c\).

Multiply by \(e^{y}\):
\(x = -(y + 1) + c\,e^{y}\).

The general solution is \(x + y + 1 = c\,e^{y}\).

The equation is \((x + a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3y = (x + a)^5\).

Divide by \((x + a)\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{3}{x + a}\,y = (x + a)^4\).

This is linear with \(P = -\dfrac{3}{x + a}\), \(Q = (x + a)^4\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -\frac{3}{x + a}dx} = e^{-3\log(x + a)} = (x + a)^{-3}\).

The solution is
\(y\,(x + a)^{-3} = \int (x + a)^4\,(x + a)^{-3}\,dx + c = \int (x + a)\,dx + c = \dfrac{(x + a)^2}{2} + c\).

Hence the general solution is
\(\dfrac{y}{(x + a)^3} = \dfrac{(x + a)^2}{2} + c\), i.e. \(y = \dfrac{(x + a)^5}{2} + c\,(x + a)^3\).

The equation is \(dr + (2r\cot\theta + \sin 2\theta)\,d\theta = 0\).

Write it as
\(\dfrac{dr}{d\theta} + (2\cot\theta)\,r = -\sin 2\theta\).

This is linear in \(r\) with \(P = 2\cot\theta\), \(Q = -\sin 2\theta\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int 2\cot\theta\,d\theta} = e^{2\log|\sin\theta|} = \sin^2\theta\).

The solution is
\(r\sin^2\theta = \int -\sin 2\theta\,\sin^2\theta\,d\theta + c\).

Since \(\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\),
\(-\sin 2\theta\,\sin^2\theta = -2\sin^3\theta\cos\theta\).

Put \(t = \sin\theta\), \(dt = \cos\theta\,d\theta\):
\(\int -2\sin^3\theta\cos\theta\,d\theta = -2\int t^3\,dt = -\dfrac{t^4}{2} = -\dfrac{\sin^4\theta}{2}\).

Hence the general solution is
\(r\sin^2\theta = -\dfrac{\sin^4\theta}{2} + c\).

We verify that \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\) is a solution of \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + r\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = y\).

Differentiate \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\) with respect to \(x\):
\(2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}\).

Now substitute into the left side of the given equation.

First, \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\left(-\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = -\dfrac{x^2}{y}\).

Next,
\(1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{x^2}{y^2} = \dfrac{y^2 + x^2}{y^2} = \dfrac{r^2}{y^2}\),
so \(\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = \dfrac{r}{|y|} = \dfrac{r}{y}\) (taking \(y > 0\)).

Hence \(r\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = \dfrac{r^2}{y}\).

Adding,
\(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + r\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = -\dfrac{x^2}{y} + \dfrac{r^2}{y} = \dfrac{r^2 - x^2}{y} = \dfrac{y^2}{y} = y\).

This equals the right side \(y\). Hence \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\) is a solution of the differential equation.

We verify that \(y = e^{ax}\sin bx\) is a solution of \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2a\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (a^2 + b^2)\,y = 0\).

Differentiate:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = a\,e^{ax}\sin bx + b\,e^{ax}\cos bx = e^{ax}(a\sin bx + b\cos bx)\).

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = a\,e^{ax}(a\sin bx + b\cos bx) + e^{ax}(ab\cos bx - b^2\sin bx)\)
\(= e^{ax}\left[(a^2 - b^2)\sin bx + 2ab\cos bx\right]\).

Now form the left side:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2a\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (a^2 + b^2)y\)
\(= e^{ax}\big[(a^2 - b^2)\sin bx + 2ab\cos bx\big] - 2a\,e^{ax}(a\sin bx + b\cos bx) + (a^2 + b^2)e^{ax}\sin bx\).

Collect the coefficient of \(e^{ax}\sin bx\):
\((a^2 - b^2) - 2a^2 + (a^2 + b^2) = a^2 - b^2 - 2a^2 + a^2 + b^2 = 0\).

Collect the coefficient of \(e^{ax}\cos bx\):
\(2ab - 2ab = 0\).

Hence the left side is \(0\), which equals the right side. Therefore \(y = e^{ax}\sin bx\) is a solution of the differential equation.

[Textbook misprint: the first term should be \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) (Cauchy–Euler form), not \(x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\).]

We verify that \(y = 3\cos(\log x) + 4\sin(\log x)\) is a solution of \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

(Note: the standard form of this equation is \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\); we work with that.)

Differentiate:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -3\sin(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} + 4\cos(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x}\left[-3\sin(\log x) + 4\cos(\log x)\right]\).

So \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -3\sin(\log x) + 4\cos(\log x)\).

Differentiate \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\).

Also
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[-3\sin(\log x) + 4\cos(\log x)\right] = -3\cos(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} - 4\sin(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x}\left[-3\cos(\log x) - 4\sin(\log x)\right] = -\dfrac{y}{x}\).

Hence
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\dfrac{y}{x}\).

Multiply through by \(x\):
\(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -y\), i.e. \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

This is the standard Cauchy–Euler form. (The equation as printed in the book shows (xdfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}) as its first term — an apparent misprint for (x^2dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}).) Hence the function is a solution of the intended equation.

[Textbook misprint: the differential equation as printed does not verify for the given function.]

We verify that \(y = ae^{x} + be^{-x} + x^2\) is a solution of \(x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x^3 = xy + 2\).

Differentiate:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = ae^{x} - be^{-x} + 2x\).

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = ae^{x} + be^{-x} + 2\).

Compute the left side:
\(x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x^3\)
\(= x(ae^{x} + be^{-x} + 2) + 2(ae^{x} - be^{-x} + 2x) + x^3\)
\(= axe^{x} + bxe^{-x} + 2x + 2ae^{x} - 2be^{-x} + 4x + x^3\)
\(= axe^{x} + bxe^{-x} + 2ae^{x} - 2be^{-x} + 6x + x^3\).

Compute the right side:
\(xy + 2 = x(ae^{x} + be^{-x} + x^2) + 2 = axe^{x} + bxe^{-x} + x^3 + 2\).

Subtract the right side from the left side:
\((axe^{x} + bxe^{-x} + 2ae^{x} - 2be^{-x} + 6x + x^3) - (axe^{x} + bxe^{-x} + x^3 + 2)\)
\(= 2ae^{x} - 2be^{-x} + 6x - 2\).

This is not identically zero, so with the equation as printed the two sides do not agree in general. The given function therefore does not satisfy the differential equation exactly as stated (there appears to be a mis-transcription in the equation). Verification cannot be completed for the printed form.

We verify that \(x^2 = 2y^2\log y\) is a solution of \(x^2 + y^2 = xy\dfrac{dx}{dy}\).

Differentiate \(x^2 = 2y^2\log y\) with respect to \(y\):
\(2x\dfrac{dx}{dy} = 2\left[2y\log y + y^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{y}\right] = 2\left[2y\log y + y\right] = 4y\log y + 2y\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dx}{dy} = 2y\log y + y\).

Multiply by \(y\):
\(xy\dfrac{dx}{dy} = 2y^2\log y + y^2\).

Now use the given relation \(2y^2\log y = x^2\):
\(xy\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x^2 + y^2\).

This is exactly the given differential equation, so \(x^2 = 2y^2\log y\) is a solution.

The equation is \(\log\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 2x + 3y\).

Take the exponential of both sides:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x + 3y} = e^{2x}\cdot e^{3y}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{dy}{e^{3y}} = e^{2x}\,dx\), i.e. \(e^{-3y}\,dy = e^{2x}\,dx\).

Integrate both sides:
\(\int e^{-3y}\,dy = \int e^{2x}\,dx\).
\(-\dfrac{1}{3}e^{-3y} = \dfrac{1}{2}e^{2x} + c_1\).

Multiply by \(-6\):
\(2e^{-3y} = -3e^{2x} + c\).

The general solution is \(3e^{2x} + 2e^{-3y} = c\).

The equation is \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 y + y = y(x^2 + 1)\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{dy}{y} = (x^2 + 1)\,dx\).

Integrate both sides:
\(\int \dfrac{dy}{y} = \int (x^2 + 1)\,dx\).
\(\log|y| = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + x + c\).

The general solution is \(\log|y| = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + x + c\).

The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2y - x}{2y + x}\) is homogeneous.

Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{2vx - x}{2vx + x} = \dfrac{2v - 1}{2v + 1}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{2v - 1}{2v + 1} - v = \dfrac{2v - 1 - v(2v + 1)}{2v + 1} = \dfrac{2v - 1 - 2v^2 - v}{2v + 1} = \dfrac{-2v^2 + v - 1}{2v + 1}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{2v + 1}{-2v^2 + v - 1}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\), i.e. \(-\dfrac{2v + 1}{2v^2 - v + 1}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\).

The derivative of the denominator \(2v^2 - v + 1\) is \(4v - 1\). Write the numerator as a multiple of this plus a constant:
\(2v + 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}(4v - 1) + \dfrac{3}{2}\).

So
\(-\int\dfrac{2v + 1}{2v^2 - v + 1}\,dv = -\dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{4v - 1}{2v^2 - v + 1}\,dv - \dfrac{3}{2}\int\dfrac{dv}{2v^2 - v + 1}\).

First integral: \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\log(2v^2 - v + 1)\).

Second integral: complete the square. \(2v^2 - v + 1 = 2\left[\left(v - \dfrac14\right)^2 + \dfrac{7}{16}\right]\), so
\(\int\dfrac{dv}{2v^2 - v + 1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{dv}{\left(v - \frac14\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt7}{4}\right)^2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{4}{\sqrt7}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{v - \frac14}{\frac{\sqrt7}{4}}\right) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt7}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{4v - 1}{\sqrt7}\right)\).

Hence
\(-\dfrac{1}{2}\log(2v^2 - v + 1) - \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{\sqrt7}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{4v - 1}{\sqrt7}\right) = \log|x| + c_1\).

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\), so \(2v^2 - v + 1 = \dfrac{2y^2 - xy + x^2}{x^2}\):
\(-\dfrac{1}{2}\log\dfrac{2y^2 - xy + x^2}{x^2} - \dfrac{3}{\sqrt7}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{4y - x}{\sqrt7\,x}\right) = \log|x| + c_1\).

Since \(-\dfrac12\log\dfrac{2y^2 - xy + x^2}{x^2} = -\dfrac12\log(2y^2 - xy + x^2) + \log|x|\), the \(\log|x|\) terms cancel, giving the general solution
\(\dfrac{1}{2}\log(x^2 - xy + 2y^2) + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt7}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{4y - x}{\sqrt7\,x}\right) = c\).

The equation \(x\,dy = (x + y + 1)\,dx\) gives
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y + 1}{x} = 1 + \dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x}\).

Rearrange into linear form:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{x}\,y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\).

This is linear with \(P = -\dfrac{1}{x}\), \(Q = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -\frac{1}{x}dx} = e^{-\log x} = \dfrac{1}{x}\).

The solution is
\(y\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} = \int\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx + c = \int\left(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)dx + c\).

Integrate:
\(\dfrac{y}{x} = \log|x| - \dfrac{1}{x} + c\).

Multiply by \(x\): the general solution is
\(y = x\log|x| - 1 + c\,x\).

The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\cot x = x^2\cot x + 2x\) is linear with \(P = \cot x\), \(Q = x^2\cot x + 2x\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \cot x\,dx} = e^{\log|\sin x|} = \sin x\).

The solution is
\(y\sin x = \int (x^2\cot x + 2x)\sin x\,dx + c\).

Simplify the integrand:
\((x^2\cot x + 2x)\sin x = x^2\cos x + 2x\sin x\).

Notice \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2\sin x) = 2x\sin x + x^2\cos x\), which is exactly this integrand. Hence
\(\int (x^2\cos x + 2x\sin x)\,dx = x^2\sin x\).

Therefore
\(y\sin x = x^2\sin x + c\).

The general solution is \(y\sin x = x^2\sin x + c\), i.e. \(y = x^2 + c\,\csc x\).

The equation is \(y\log y = (\log y^2 - x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), i.e. \(y\log y = (2\log y - x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Write it as a linear equation in \(x\) (treating \(x\) as a function of \(y\)):
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{2\log y - x}{y\log y} = \dfrac{2}{y} - \dfrac{x}{y\log y}\).

So
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} + \dfrac{1}{y\log y}\,x = \dfrac{2}{y}\).

This is linear in \(x\) with \(P = \dfrac{1}{y\log y}\), \(Q = \dfrac{2}{y}\).

Integrating factor:
\(\int \dfrac{1}{y\log y}\,dy\). Put \(t = \log y\), \(dt = \dfrac{1}{y}dy\): \(\int\dfrac{dt}{t} = \log|t| = \log|\log y|\).
So \(\text{I.F.} = e^{\log|\log y|} = \log y\).

The solution is
\(x\log y = \int \dfrac{2}{y}\log y\,dy + c\).

With \(t = \log y\), \(\dfrac{2}{y}\log y\,dy = 2t\,dt\), so \(\int 2t\,dt = t^2 = (\log y)^2\).

Hence the general solution is
\(x\log y = (\log y)^2 + c\).

The equation is \(4\dfrac{dx}{dy} + 8x = 5e^{-3y}\).

Divide by 4:
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} + 2x = \dfrac{5}{4}e^{-3y}\).

This is linear in \(x\) with \(P = 2\), \(Q = \dfrac{5}{4}e^{-3y}\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int 2\,dy} = e^{2y}\).

The solution is
\(x\,e^{2y} = \int \dfrac{5}{4}e^{-3y}\cdot e^{2y}\,dy + c = \dfrac{5}{4}\int e^{-y}\,dy + c = \dfrac{5}{4}(-e^{-y}) + c\).

Hence
\(x\,e^{2y} = -\dfrac{5}{4}e^{-y} + c\).

Multiply by \(e^{-2y}\):
\(x = -\dfrac{5}{4}e^{-3y} + c\,e^{-2y}\).

The general solution is \(x = c\,e^{-2y} - \dfrac{5}{4}e^{-3y}\).

The equation is \(y(1 + \log x) = (\log x^{x})\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Since \(\log x^{x} = x\log x\), write
\(y(1 + \log x) = x\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{1 + \log x}{x\log x}\,dx\).

For the right side, note that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\log x) = \log x + 1\), and the denominator is \(x\log x\). So the right side is \(\dfrac{d(x\log x)}{x\log x}\). Integrating,
\(\int\dfrac{dy}{y} = \int\dfrac{d(x\log x)}{x\log x}\).
\(\log|y| = \log|x\log x| + \log c\).

Hence \(y = c\,x\log x\).

Apply the condition \(y(e) = e^{2}\): at \(x = e\), \(\log e = 1\), so
\(e^{2} = c\cdot e\cdot 1 = ce\), giving \(c = e\).

The particular solution is \(y = e\,x\log x\).

The equation \((x + 2y^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\) is linear in \(x\).

Write
\(\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x + 2y^2}{y} = \dfrac{x}{y} + 2y\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1}{y}\,x = 2y\).

This is linear with \(P = -\dfrac{1}{y}\), \(Q = 2y\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -\frac{1}{y}dy} = e^{-\log y} = \dfrac{1}{y}\).

The solution is
\(x\cdot\dfrac{1}{y} = \int 2y\cdot\dfrac{1}{y}\,dy + c = \int 2\,dy + c = 2y + c\).

So \(\dfrac{x}{y} = 2y + c\), i.e. \(x = 2y^2 + cy\).

Apply the condition \(x = 2\), \(y = 1\):
\(2 = 2(1)^2 + c(1) = 2 + c\), so \(c = 0\).

The particular solution is \(x = 2y^2\).

The equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3y\cot x = \sin 2x\) is linear with \(P = -3\cot x\), \(Q = \sin 2x\).

Integrating factor:
\(\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -3\cot x\,dx} = e^{-3\log|\sin x|} = \dfrac{1}{\sin^3 x}\).

The solution is
\(y\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin^3 x} = \int \sin 2x\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin^3 x}\,dx + c\).

Since \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\),
\(\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sin^3 x} = \dfrac{2\sin x\cos x}{\sin^3 x} = \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\).

Put \(t = \sin x\), \(dt = \cos x\,dx\):
\(\int \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\,dx = 2\int \dfrac{dt}{t^2} = -\dfrac{2}{t} = -\dfrac{2}{\sin x}\).

Hence
\(\dfrac{y}{\sin^3 x} = -\dfrac{2}{\sin x} + c\), i.e. \(y = -2\sin^2 x + c\sin^3 x\).

Apply the condition \(y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2\): at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(\sin x = 1\), so
\(2 = -2(1) + c(1) = -2 + c\), giving \(c = 4\).

The particular solution is \(y = -2\sin^2 x + 4\sin^3 x\).

The equation \((x + y)\,dy + (x - y)\,dx = 0\) gives
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x - y}{x + y} = \dfrac{y - x}{x + y}\).

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then
\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{vx - x}{x + vx} = \dfrac{v - 1}{1 + v}\).

So
\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v - 1}{1 + v} - v = \dfrac{v - 1 - v(1 + v)}{1 + v} = \dfrac{v - 1 - v - v^2}{1 + v} = \dfrac{-(1 + v^2)}{1 + v}\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{1 + v}{1 + v^2}\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Split the left side:
\(\int\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + v^2} + \dfrac{v}{1 + v^2}\right)dv = -\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\).
\(\tan^{-1} v + \dfrac{1}{2}\log(1 + v^2) = -\log|x| + c\).

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\), \(1 + v^2 = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x^2}\):
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{1}{2}\log\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x^2} = -\log|x| + c\).

Since \(\dfrac{1}{2}\log\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x^2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\log(x^2 + y^2) - \log|x|\), the \(\log|x|\) terms cancel:
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{1}{2}\log(x^2 + y^2) = c\).

Apply the condition \(x = 1\), \(y = 1\):
\(\tan^{-1} 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\log 2 = c\), so \(c = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\).

The particular solution is
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{1}{2}\log(x^2 + y^2) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\).

[Textbook misprint: the equation as printed does not match the book's own answer key; the intended homogeneous form is solved below.]

Note: as printed, \(2e^{x/y}\,dx + \left(y - 2xe^{x/y}\right)dy = 0\) does not integrate in closed form and does not match the book's answer key. The equation the book intends (the one its answer \(x + 2ye^{x/y} = 2\) solves) is the homogeneous form \(y\left(1 + 2e^{x/y}\right)dx + 2e^{x/y}(y - x)\,dy = 0\); we solve that.

Put \(x = vy\), so \(dx = v\,dy + y\,dv\) and \(e^{x/y} = e^{v}\). Substituting reduces the equation to \((v + 2e^{v})\,dy + y(1 + 2e^{v})\,dv = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{y} = -\dfrac{(1 + 2e^{v})\,dv}{v + 2e^{v}}\).

Since \(d(v + 2e^{v}) = (1 + 2e^{v})\,dv\), integrating gives \(\log|y| = -\log\left|v + 2e^{v}\right| + \text{const}\), so \(y(v + 2e^{v}) = c\). With \(v = \dfrac{x}{y}\): \(x + 2ye^{x/y} = c\).

Apply \(y(0) = 1\), i.e. \(x = 0,\ y = 1\): \(0 + 2(1)e^{0} = 2 = c\).

\(\therefore\) the particular solution is \(x + 2ye^{x/y} = 2\).

[Textbook error: the general solution stated in the question carries a sign error; the correct family is derived below.]

We are to show the general solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2 + y + 1}{x^2 + x + 1}\) is \((x + y + 1) = c(1 - x - y - 2xy)\).

Separate the variables:
\(\dfrac{dy}{y^2 + y + 1} = \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + x + 1}\).

Complete the square in each denominator: \(y^2 + y + 1 = \left(y + \dfrac12\right)^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}\) and \(x^2 + x + 1 = \left(x + \dfrac12\right)^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}\), with \(\dfrac34 = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2\).

Integrate both sides using \(\int\dfrac{dt}{t^2 + a^2} = \dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{t}{a}\):
\(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2y + 1}{\sqrt3}\right) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2x + 1}{\sqrt3}\right) + \text{const}\).

Multiply by \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\):
\(\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2y + 1}{\sqrt3}\right) - \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2x + 1}{\sqrt3}\right) = k\),
where \(k\) is a constant.

Use \(\tan^{-1}A - \tan^{-1}B = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{A - B}{1 + AB}\), with \(A = \dfrac{2y + 1}{\sqrt3}\), \(B = \dfrac{2x + 1}{\sqrt3}\):

\(A - B = \dfrac{(2y + 1) - (2x + 1)}{\sqrt3} = \dfrac{2(y - x)}{\sqrt3}\).

\(1 + AB = 1 + \dfrac{(2y + 1)(2x + 1)}{3} = \dfrac{3 + (4xy + 2x + 2y + 1)}{3} = \dfrac{4xy + 2x + 2y + 4}{3} = \dfrac{2(2xy + x + y + 2)}{3}\).

So
\(\dfrac{A - B}{1 + AB} = \dfrac{2(y - x)/\sqrt3}{2(2xy + x + y + 2)/3} = \dfrac{3(y - x)}{\sqrt3\,(2xy + x + y + 2)} = \dfrac{\sqrt3\,(y - x)}{2xy + x + y + 2}\).

Therefore
\(\tan^{-1}\!\left[\dfrac{\sqrt3\,(y - x)}{2xy + x + y + 2}\right] = k\), i.e. \(\dfrac{\sqrt3\,(y - x)}{2xy + x + y + 2} = \tan k\), a constant.

Hence the general solution is
\(y - x = c\,(2xy + x + y + 2)\)
for an arbitrary constant \(c\). One can verify directly by implicit differentiation that this family satisfies \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^{2} + y + 1}{x^{2} + x + 1}\).

This is the required general solution. (The form printed in the book, \((x + y + 1) = c(1 - x - y - 2xy)\), carries a sign error: it fails the differential equation — for instance at the origin it forces slope \(-1\) whereas the equation gives \(+1\). The correct family is \(y - x = c(2xy + x + y + 2)\), derived above.)
